newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open flat to 0.05 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open flat to 0.05 lower.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open unchanged to 0.05 cent per lb weaker on Monday, traders said.

Friday, the most-active July contract settled 0.04 cent lower at 11.17 cents per lb, having traded from 11.15 to 11.25 cents. October closed down 0.01 cent at 11.00 cents, while the rest of the board was finished the day unchanged to 0.02 lower.
In fundamental news, Iran today bought 30,000 tonnes of raw sugar for about $280 per tonne, for shipment in August, trading sources said.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture on Friday pegged 1997/98 world sugar consumption at a record 125 million tonnes.
LIFFE white sugar futures were narrowly mixed on Monday. At 0845 EDT/1245 GMT, the spot-August contract stood $0.20 cent lower at $323.90, and the rest of the board was $1.40 to $0.10 firmer.
